statement: What value of $x$ satisfies the equation $\sqrt[3]{x - 5} = -2$?

choices.misconception: I multiplied $-2$ by $3$ instead of cubing it, so I solved $x - 5 = -6$.
I squared $-2$ instead of cubing it, so I solved $x - 5 = 4$.
I cubed $2$ instead of $-2$, so I solved $x - 5 = 8$.

hints: Undo a cube root by cubing both sides.

solutions.reliable: Cubing both sides gives $x - 5 = (-2)^3 = -8$, so $x = -3$. Check: $\sqrt[3]{-3 - 5} = \sqrt[3]{-8} = -2$. Unlike a square root, a cube root can be negative, so there is nothing to reject.
